subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB339 LANDED. GR4a and GR4b's ORDER and PLACEMENT were already conforming and stay so: both READ emitters run the implicit MOVE only inside the success branch, after the record-area splice and after the GR15 length store, so 'the same READ statement without the INTO phrase is executed' first (GR4a) and item identification of identifier-1 happens after the read (GR4b); GR5's unsuccessful-READ arm is pinned by conformance:cases/14.9.30-READ/l1_read_into_unsuccessful. WHAT WAS DEFECTIVE AND IS NOW FIXED, both halves of GR4b's middle sentences: (1) THE SENDER SIZE. 'The size of the current record is determined by rules specified in the RECORD clause' (cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 => OK 4) b)) sends the reader to 13.18.43.4 GR16 (--check 13.18.43.4 'the number of bytes in the current record that participate as the sending operands in the implicit MOVE statement is determined by the following conditions' => OK 16)), whose a) arm is data-name-1's content and whose b) arm is 'the value that would have been moved into the data item referenced by data-name-1 had data-name-1 been specified' (--check => OK 16)). Both emitters used to send the WHOLE space-padded record area; the sender is now a BoundCurrentRecord operand rendering CobolString.RefMod(<record-area image>, 1, <GR16 count>) with allowZeroLength (GR16's closing 'If the number of bytes determined as above is zero, the record is a zero-length item', --check => OK 16)), the GR16 a) count read through the same renderer GR13 a) uses and the GR16 b) count read from the connector's last-read length. (2) THE GROUP-MOVE DESIGNATION. 'If the file description entry contains a RECORD IS VARYING clause, the implied move is an alphanumeric group move' (--check 14.9.30.4 => OK 4) b)) was not applied at all: MoveClassifier saw only the record area's own level structure, so a FORMAT 2 FD with an elementary 01 EDITED into an alphanumeric-edited receiver and CONVERTED into a numeric-edited one. MoveClassifier.IsGroupSender now honours the designation, so 14.9.25.4 GR4's 'treated exactly as if it were an alphanumeric to alphanumeric elementary move, except that there is no conversion of data from one form of internal representation to another' (--check 14.9.25.4 => OK 4)) governs. FORMAT 3 (RECORD CONTAINS m TO n) is deliberately NOT given the designation - GR4b conditions it on the WORD VARYING, and GR16 is stated under the FORMAT 2 heading - which is why VaryingRecordInfo now records which format was written. GOLDEN pb339_into_current_record, identical at all four editions (no Annex E change touches GR4b, GR16, or the JUSTIFIED clause), seven derived legs: A a 5-byte record into PIC X(10) JUSTIFIED => '     ABCDE' (13.18.32.4 GR2, --check => OK 2)); B into PIC X(3) JUSTIFIED => 'CDE' (GR1's leftmost truncation, --check => OK 1)); C into PIC X(10) => 'ABCDE     ' (the control leg, identical before and after); D into PIC XXBXXBXX => 'ABCDE   ' (the group-move designation - no editing); E into PIC X(3) => 'ABC'; F the GR16 b) arm - a two-record FD with no DEPENDING ON phrase, WRITE of the short 01 then READ INTO PIC X(10) JUSTIFIED => '     ABCDE'; G the RETURN twin, 14.9.34.4 GR5 b), through the same builder. Before the fix A/B/F printed only spaces and D printed the edited '12 34 56' shape. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 . 2002 . 2014 . 2023 || kb/Work PB348 (code-location only): the INTO sender builder moved from SequentialIoEmitter.IntoSender to MoveBinder.BindIntoPhrase when the implicit move of every INTO phrase became a BOUND sub-statement instead of an emitter-built node. The rule, the verdict and the evidence are unchanged; only the address is. The rename rides a batch rather than a hand edit because the lander re-applies batches on the merged tree and drops hand edits to the inventory JSON.
